data.text/markdown:
Weight-edit minimization — run the experiments yourself

Two campaigns asked the same question: what is the smallest set of weights whose edit produces a behavior? Both start from an edit written by Astra (RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs) and strip it down. This notebook is the experiment, not a report about it. Run the cells top to bottom (▷ Run all, bottom right). Each experiment is a short code cell, and the charts under it fill in as runs finish, next to the numbers the original orx runs recorded. Change a variable and rerun to try your own version. Collapsed cells hold plumbing (setup, the Kinetix harness, chart helpers); click one to read it. Time. Section 1 runs about 20 evaluations of 256 episodes each on the CPU: ~5 minutes on a laptop. Section 2's analysis is instant; running Qwen yourself (§2.5) is off until you set RUN_QWEN = True.

1 · Car-ramp: a PPO actor that never solves its level, fixed by 10–12 weights

Kinetix l/h2_car_ramp: get the car's green wheel over the ramp and into the blue goal without the green wheel touching the red strip. A PPO actor trained for 1.001 B steps never does it. Astra's hand-written edit changes 6,073 of its weights and solves it every time. How many of those 6,073 matter?

1.1 Settings and the base network

Every evaluation below uses these settings. The orx runs used 256 episodes for the audits and 1,024 for the headline numbers; sampled episodes use the same key schedule as eval_actor.py, so with the same episode count and seed you get exactly the recorded counts.
171,664 actor weights in 14 tensors

The actor is a ReLU embedding (679 observations → 128 units), five tanh layers of 128, and a head of 16 action logits (only the first 3 drive the motor). The cell below (collapsed) is the evaluation harness: the exact tools/eval_actor.py the orx runs used, on official Kinetix (kinetix-env==3.0.2, JAX on CPU). It gives you evaluate(weights, episodes, seed), trace_episode(weights) for one recorded episode, and animate(...).
1.2 Experiment: does the base network solve the level?

base PPO: solved 0/256 · hit red 0% · timed out 100% · mean episode 256 steps · 14.4 s
recorded orx run (1024 episodes, seed 0): 0/1024, mean 256 steps

It drives toward the goal, climbs onto the ramp and stalls there until the episode times out. It never backs up: at the start p(reverse) ≈ 10⁻¹².

Astra zeroed most of embed columns 6, 7 and 8, turning three dead ReLU units into clean single-input taps for car x, car vx and green-wheel x. Undo one column's erasures at a time:

1.7 Look inside: what the 12 entries do

Trace one episode and watch the units the edit wires together. Unit L:u is the tanh output of actor{L} unit u. In greedy-12, PPO's own speed detector 0:122 feeds a gate 1:126, which drives a relay 2:126; 0:127 is a green-wheel comparator. For C2-min try 0:23, 1:29, 2:105, 4:73.

data.text/markdown:
2 · Experiment 8: Qwen3.5-0.8B math edit, and how much of it is needed

Astra's p50c edit makes Qwen3.5-0.8B stop looping on math (MATH-500 7.9% → 48.1% in the published evaluation). It changes 130,188 bf16 entries of layers.{15,19}.mlp.down_proj.weight (1024 × 3584 each). The minimal-edit campaign built 27 subsets of it and screened each on the same 256 MATH-train problems (vLLM, thinking on, temp 0.6, 32k tokens, one sample each). Those screens ran on a GPU and are bundled as raw per-problem outputs; the analysis below recomputes everything from them, and §2.5 lets you run the model yourself.

2.1 Apply Astra's edit and recover what it is
layer 15: 65,260 entries changed · layer 19: 64,928 entries changed

data.text/html: The change is rank-1: one direction u subtracted through 64 MLP neurons per layer, the same direction in both layers (|cos(u₁₅, u₁₉)| = 0.849). Astra's exact u is not in the logs, so u here is estimated from Δ after bf16 rounding; that reproduces 98–99% of the touched entries to within one rounding step, and Astra's run checked the formula against its exact u (last row).

Which neurons did Astra edit? Neuron j writes the direction with strength |u·W₀[:, j]|. Astra did not take the 64 strongest writers: it ranked by strength × how much more the neuron fires on looping text (its notes, data/docs/exp8/notes_astra_method.md). layer 15: 31 of the 64 are among the 64 strongest writers, the weakest ranks 1,114; layer 19: 18 of the 64 are among the 64 strongest writers, the weakest ranks 2,420. Hover a point for its neuron number.

data.text/markdown:
2.2 Experiment: build the campaign's 27 candidates

Each candidate keeps part of Astra's edit: the top-k neurons (A), the B largest entries per layer (D), the top-R output rows of layer 15 (ER), or one layer only (B). make_spec regenerates the specs from the saved factors; build_bits applies them. The check: same specs and same entry counts as the campaign.

2.5 Run the model yourself

Paired generations, unedited base vs a candidate, on the first screening problems, with the campaign's chat template, thinking on, and sampling (temp 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20). Needs an Apple-silicon GPU or CUDA (CPU runs at ~0.5 tokens/s) and downloads Qwen3.5-0.8B (~1.7 GB) once. On an M-series Mac, 8 problems × 1,024 tokens takes ~1.5 min. What to expect. At laptop budgets both versions are still thinking when they are cut off, so accuracy barely moves. The edit's effect shows at the campaign's 32k cap (base cut off on 91% of problems, full edit 30%), so the table also shows each problem's recorded 32k screening.
